name: How much should I budget for a high-end home remodel in LA?

mainEntity.name: How much should I budget for a high-end home remodel in LA?
mainEntity.text: How much should I budget for a high-end home remodel in LA?

acceptedAnswer.text: A high-end Los Angeles remodel should be budgeted as a full project cost, not just a construction number. That means design fees, engineering, permits, demolition, labor, premium materials, fixtures, cabinetry, and a contingency reserve should all be included. Luxury projects also tend to have more custom work, longer lead times, and more coordination, which increases carrying costs. Many homeowners forget the hidden budget items: temporary housing, storage, moving, utility changes, and tax or fee implications tied to the property. A strong budgeting approach is to build the project from scope first, then add a contingency for surprises, especially in older homes where plumbing, electrical, foundation, or framing issues can emerge after demolition. If you are comparing bids, make sure each quote includes the same allowances for tile, stone, appliances, lighting, and hardware. Otherwise, a lower bid may simply be missing real costs. In luxury remodeling, the quality of execution and the clarity of allowances matter as much as the headline price. The safest budget is the one that assumes a few surprises and still protects finish quality.
acceptedAnswer.description: High-end home remodels in Los Angeles often cost far more than basic updates because of labor, design complexity, and premium finishes. Budgeting should usually include construction, design, permits, contingency, and temporary living costs if the home is uninhabitable during work.
